U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.

features.description: Recognize æ, interchangeable manuscript þ/ð, Cook's preference for ð, his hooked ę, and quantity marks; preserve exact printed quantities.
Distinguish long vowels/diphthongs from syllable weight due to two consonants or a geminate; apply only the stated noun-pattern domains.
Use the assigned lexical gender; do not infer it from English or from a bare nominative ending alone.
Identical spellings may occupy different case/number cells; determine syntactic role from construction and agreement.
Coordinate nominal phrases with and; each article agrees with its own head.
Strong masculine consonant stems: complete N/G/D/A singular and plural; assign only the listed lexical senses.
Strong masculine -e: replace the nominative -e appropriately; no invented mętees.
Complete dæg and hwæl patterns, with æ in singular and a in plural; do not extend to clusters such as wæstm.
Complete selected fugol and morgen patterns; loss of medial vowel with endings and lexical diagnostic forms. Source variants remain valid.
Complete hof and sǣd patterns; short-stem monosyllabic neuter N/A plural -u versus heavy-stem zero; explain geminates and clusters.
Complete trēo paradigm with w before endings and selected exceptional N/A plural trēowu.
Complete selected ǣfen, tācen, wæter, nīeten patterns; retain or syncopate medial vowel as documented, not by an unrestricted weight rule.
Complete long-stem strong feminine pattern; selected N/A plural -a, with source -e variants noted separately.
Complete selected tīd and wyrt patterns; endingless accusative singular despite ordinary -e feminine obliques.
Complete -nes pattern; -ness- in obliques/plural, retaining e; apply to each listed diagnostic stem.
Complete selected -ung/-ing feminine pattern, productive -e singular obliques; source -a variants separately noted.
Complete weak masculine steorra and weak feminine eorðe patterns; contrast all singular/plural cases.
Complete mann: męnn dative singular and nominative/accusative plural; other selected cases as listed.
Complete selected niht paradigm, including genitive singular niht and endingless nominative/accusative plural.
Complete selected sea table, with productive attested cells and explicitly supplied reconstructed genitive plural *sǣwa.
Complete selected plural-only darkness paradigm; no singular invented.
Produce the selected article forms agreeing with their own noun in gender, number and nominative/genitive/dative/accusative case.
Recognize distinct instrumental masculine/neuter singular ðȳ and ðon as reference cells; no productive instrumental syntax.
Produce every person/number cell of the present eom/eart/is/sindon and preterite wæs/wǣre/wæs/wǣron indicative series.
Finite subjects and noun predicates identifying the subject are nominative; ordinary bare noun predicates need no translated indefinite article.
Use the copula's appropriate number/person in the taught ordinary clauses.
Produce limiting relational genitives. Follow Cook's exercise target: dependent first, head noun without its own article; retain the dependent's required article.
Select accusative direct-object noun/article forms in explicitly supplied transitive finite-verb frames.
Use taught locative on with dative ('in/on'); this is a selected construction, not a universal spatial rule.
Use fram plus dative for the entity from which something is separated, in an explicitly supplied separating frame.
